articles.title: Location-tracking apps have turned me into a gibbering wreck – but I just can’t look away
articles.summary: When my loved ones are on the move, I can’t rest until I know they’ve got from A to B safely. How I long for the ignorance of the olden days. I’ll call it compassionate surveillance. It’s what I do when I’m worried about a loved one who is on the move. I’m not sure it’s a good thing.
body: I cross my heart and hope to die when I swear to you that I only do this when they are in transit. Honestly, I never look up where they are on a night out or whatever. That would be weird – or weirder, anyway. But when they get in a car, I get the fear. The catastrophising begins. It’s a big world and their car is small. A million other cars, buses and lorries share the roads on which they are motoring. In this, as in all things, overthinking is calamitous. The more you think about what could go wrong, the more your imagination obliges with a steady stream of ghastly possibilities.

The answer is simple: stop being an idiot, stop torturing yourself, stop thinking about it and think about something else. Sometimes, I achieve this. More often, I don’t. I resist the temptation to check the tech for as long as possible, but invariably I give in. I’ve yet to find anything absorbing enough to distract me from the paranoia. I can be sitting at a football match, in a live radio studio, in an intense conversation, and that will work only for a while before a sick feeling strikes and I’m wondering if my loved ones are all right.

articles.title: Are you cleaning your cat litter box correctly?
articles.summary: How often should you clean your cat’s litter box? Plus three other tips for peak cat cleanliness. Throughout history, people have revered cats. Ancient Egyptians worshipped feline deities. In Norse mythology, the Viking goddess Freya rode around in a sled pulled by two cats.
body: As anyone who has lived with a cat knows, we serve them and not the other way around. This includes the messy and malodorous task of tending their litter box.

According to experts, there is often room for improvement. “The most common mistake people make when it comes to their cat’s litter is creating a setup that works for them instead of for the cat,” says Samantha Bell, cat expert and content strategist for the non-profit rescue Best Friends Animal Society. “But we bring our cats into our homes, so we need to do our best to ensure they are as comfortable as possible, and a litter box is a huge part of their comfort.”
Below, what you need to know to ensure your feline overlord’s bathroom satisfaction.

On TikTok, I once saw someone claim cat owners should have a litter box in every room. I imagined my small apartment crammed with litter boxes and despaired. “Is that what you want?” I desperately asked my cat, who doesn’t speak English and doesn’t respect me enough to answer me even if she did.
points: How often should you clean your cat’s litter box?

articles.title: Hoy Is Bringing Night-Market Energy to NYC
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. This is the first installment of our series Getting on the Map, presented by Apple Maps.
body: When I spoke with Cyed Adraincem, he apologized for stumbling over any words; he’d been up at 4 a.m. to wash the sidewalk in front of his forthcoming restaurant. “I wanted to beat all the foot traffic,” he said.

Adraincem seems to have brought that same dedication to outfitting Hoy, which will serve Filipino street food in a Manila night-market-like space. Though not yet open, the restaurant has already garnered a lot of attention for its loud and off-kilter aesthetic, smart pop cultural ties, and behind-the-scenes peeks into R&D. I asked him about designing the space, the merch plan, and how opening is going.

Cyed Adraincem: It’s Filipino street food, super fast casual. I’m trying to introduce Filipino food to a broader audience because I feel like we’re underrepresented in New York City. We’ll be serving barbecue skewers, lumpia, and a couple different sandwiches. It’s a pretty simple menu, nothing too fancy, mostly traditional, with chef techniques that we’ve learned over the years. I think the New York dining scene wants something more casual, more affordable right now. They don’t want something pretentious; they just want to eat and have a good drink.

articles.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: pair a little skirt with a chunky jumper for the perfect balancing act
articles.summary: Let your legs enjoy the last of the summer’s breeze while a thick top or jacket keeps away the autumn chill. This is the most enjoyable time of the year to get dressed because clothes can just be clothes.
body: And this benign early part of autumn is more fun to dress for than the equivalent weather in spring, because we still have a bit of summer swagger. The summer habit of wearing shorts and halter tops and even swimwear has gotten us a little loose, a little more laid-back about flashing a bit of skin here or there. It is about more than bare flesh, though. There is something about summer that flexes the flashy dresser in everyone – whether that’s fancy dress for a festival, or just the way that putting on a pair of sunglasses brings out your inner movie star.

It is very important to hold on to that summer glow, that more fabulous version of yourself, the one who starred in your holiday snaps carousel, for as long as you can. I do this literally, getting through my bodyweight in Dove Visible Glow, my preferred slap-it-on-like-body-lotion gradual self-tan, between now and when the clocks go back. But the less literal-minded among you can hold on to that lovely golden-hour feeling in your mind, as well as in your body. Stay locked into your summer playlist and keep hold of that windows-down, shades-on spirit of freedom at least until the leaves start to turn.
points: Let your legs enjoy the last of the summer’s breeze while a thick top or jacket keeps away the autumn chill.

articles.title: ‘We thought death could do with a bit of dancing’: welcome to Sondering, the arts festival with its own funeral march
articles.summary: A brush with mortality inspired sisters Sophia and Camilla Minden to create a death-themed event featuring live bands, wild swimming … and an ‘emoshpit’ Raised in the Lake District on “music, moss and macaroni cheese,” Sophia and Camilla Minden were mindful of death from a very early age.
body: What they didn’t expect was that little more than a decade later, they’d be planning Camilla’s own funeral. Diagnosed with late-stage Hodgkin’s lymphoma just after her 20th birthday, she was given an 80% chance of survival, but the other 20% made her investigate her local undertakers (“dated, impersonal and expensive”) and work out what she wanted at her funeral (“spag bol and quite a lot of Michael Jackson”). Navigating “shit wigs” and people’s awkwardness around the subject of dying, she says that she spent a lot of time “bargaining with God”, promising that if she made it through, she’d live life to the full and appreciate every single day.

articles.title: The Story Behind Collina Strada’s First Home Collection—and Its Exuberant Garden Party Launch
articles.summary: Moments after Hillary Taymour’s spring 2027 show concluded, guests headed to a nearby field in Storm King Art Center to discover her new homewares collection with Layered.
body: Yesterday saw Hillary Taymour in her element—and not only because the Collina Strada creative director brought some 400 onlookers upstate to Storm King Art Center for her spring 2027 runway show, capped with a special performance by Carly Rae Jepsen. The after-party saw Taymour reimagine her living room (complete with her very own sofa) on a grassy knoll beyond the catwalk, where guests arrived via golf cart to discover the label’s first home collection.

Developed in collaboration with the Swedish interiors brand Layered, the drop includes a low-slung modular sofa available in two patterns: one lifted from the floor of Collina Strada’s Chinatown boutique and painted by Taymour herself, the other taken directly from a plaid shown for fall 2026. There are also four rugs, available in four standard sizes or custom-cut, again drawn from Taymour’s playful house codes and color palettes. “You have to commit, or else it doesn’t feel genuine,” she says.
points: Moments after Hillary Taymour’s spring 2027 show concluded, guests headed to a nearby field in Storm King Art Center to discover her new homewares collection with Layered.

articles.title: Watch Vogue Cover Star Michael B. Jordan in “The Fitting”
articles.summary: The fitting before a major shoot can be demanding, it can be vulnerable—but when Michael B. Jordan stopped by the Adelphi ahead of his October 2026 Vogue cover shoot, the intimacy was on another level.
body: Jordan’s favorite snack? Dried mango. His favorite hobby? Cooking. How about his favorite color? Purple. And where does he keep that aforementioned Academy Award, picked up this year for his dual leading roles as Smoke and Stack in Ryan Coogler’s Sinners? In his closet. The first role that he can remember playing? A lifetime ago, Jordan had a teeny-tiny part on The Sopranos. How about the actor that most influenced his career? He names not one, but four: Denzel Washington, Leonardo DiCaprio, Tom Hanks, and Tom Cruise. And there’s a lot more personal lore where that came from.

articles.title: Meet the Chrome Hearts Collector Who Amassed a Collection So Large He Had to Open His Own Store
articles.summary: Raphael Badalov is 22 years old and a die-hard Chrome Hearts fan who collects the brand and has opened a store to sell some of its most beloved items.
body: “I don’t collect Chrome Hearts for the sake of collecting,” says Raphael Badalov, the 22-year-old collector and founder of Byraph, home to one of the largest collections of rare Chrome Hearts items in the world. “I collect it out of respect for its value and culture, out of love for the brand, the designs, and its history.”

Long before he started collecting rare Chrome Hearts, Badalov’s infatuation with fashion began at a young age. Growing up in Brooklyn, he was inspired by streetwear culture and stores such as VFiles and Opening Ceremony, while his mother’s closet introduced him to high fashion. “I’d go into my mom’s closet and try on her Vetements and realize how transformative clothes can be,” Badalov recalls. “I realized fashion isn’t just having a cool outfit. It’s about expressing yourself. I felt like I was able to radiate my personality with confidence in a way that I couldn’t and still can’t otherwise.”

articles.title: If You Loved 'The Shards,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next
articles.summary: Craving more decadent, 1980s-themed thrills like “The Shards”? There’s a perfect movie choice for you.
body: The Shards is a classic Bret Easton Ellis story, populated by sexy, empty monsters and punctuated by horrifying imagery. The man who gave us Less Than Zero and American Psycho knows how to deliver the icy, perverse thrills that only a show set in 1980s Los Angeles (and told from his distinct point-of-view) can give us. Whether it was the hot, dangerous characters, the neon-lit visuals, or the tense mystery and mounting sense of paranoia that you loved best, if you’re looking for more of it, there’s one movie that’s perfect for Shards fans: 2008’s The Informers.

Unlike The Shards, there’s no central mystery or throughline like the Trawler. But the same sense of existential dread pervades the film—in fact, it’s easy to imagine that the Trawler is working in the background of the film’s stories, but these self-absorbed people don’t realize it because it doesn’t directly affect them. And the ending of the film is a gut punch—a horrifying moment of revelation that tells you that no matter how rich these folks are, or how attractive, or how privileged, they’re also all doomed.
